chunks: My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, all of them from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Sulayman ibn Umar from Muhajir ibn al-Hasan from Zayd ibn Arqam from The Prophet (s.a.w.s.) who said:
A person who recites Laa ilaaha illallaah with pure intention will enter Paradise. And reciting it with pure intention implies that he keeps away from what has been prohibited by Allah.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: The declaration of monotheism (There is no god but Allah)
key_terms.یَحْجُزَهُ: It acts as a barrier/restrainer for him

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of sincere declaration of monotheism (La ilaha illallah) that leads to Paradise?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that true sincerity (ikhlas) in the declaration of monotheism is evidenced by its practical function as a restraining force against divine prohibitions, linking creed directly to conduct. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unity of belief and action, where the verbal testimony is validated by its ability to curb sin and guide ethical behavior.
